The easiest way to fool someone is to give them something they already expect. A job offer. A message about a service outage. A familiar app. Nothing looks strange at first. And that's the problem. This week's stories show how ordinary things are being used to steal data, spread malware, and get people to hand over access.

There's another shift worth watching. AI is making some attacks easier to run and harder to spot. Stolen data can now be searched like a shopping catalog. Phishing emails can be tested and rewritten until they get through. At the same time, researchers are finding that even powerful AI systems have safety gaps of their own.

And while everyone is watching the new tools, the old problems haven't gone anywhere. Third-party breaches, years of hidden spying, ransomware, and security fixes still need attention. Some stories are clever. Others are painfully simple. Here's what caught our attention this week.

The threats change every week. Subscribe, and we’ll alert you when each new ThreatsDay Bulletin is out.

Google has unveiled Gemini 4 Neon, its latest frontier model capable of delivering reasoning faster and more cost-efficiently. According to the company's DeepMind division, it also produces more secure code than Carbon across all easy, medium, and hard challenges on AutoBaxBench, achieving state-of-the-art on the hard tier (76%). "Neon for cyber delivers frontier-level performance across the code hardening lifecycle — vulnerability finding, validating, and patching — all while being faster and more cost-efficient than large frontier models," Google said . "Neon achieves state-of-the-art performance on SEC-bench Pro (90.5%), while costing roughly half as much per challenge." Gemini 4 Neon for cyber is rolling out to trusted defenders in the coming days as part of the Fairwind Program.

OpenAI has introduced GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol with a "significant jump" in cyber capabilities. "They find and exploit vulnerabilities more effectively, write more secure code, and produce better patches, with substantial token-efficiency gains on several evaluations," OpenAI said. "Like GPT‑6 Astra⁠, 6.2 Astra and Sol meet the Critical threshold for cybersecurity under our Preparedness Framework⁠." The company also said it has made defensive capabilities a core focus by allowing the models to write secure code from the start. The development comes amid a disclosure from the U.K. AI Security Institute (AISI) that it developed a universal jailbreak against two pre-release versions of OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra in half the queries required for GPT-6 Astra, adding it identified a "substantial regression in jailbreak robustness relative to GPT-6 Astra." OpenAI has since addressed the regression.

WordPress has released WordPress 7.1.5 with fixes for multiple security issues. "Because this is a security release, it is recommended that you update your sites immediately," WordPress said . The patches have also been backported to all branches eligible to receive security fixes (currently through 4.7).

OpenAI will embed independent evaluators from Apollo Research, Goodfire, METR, and Transluce in its organization as part of a pilot to help support its safety work. items.content: Ripple's Alderoty doubts Elizabeth Warren will 'set crypto policy in this country,' backs durable agency rules Alderoty downplayed Warren’s influence, backing durable agency rules, and urging crypto groups to unify their message to Congress. Regulation • November 19, 2026, 1:47PM EST lev radin / Shutterstock Alderoty downplayed Elizabeth Warren’s influence and expects federal agencies to drive crypto policy. He sees little chance of a broad Clarity Act revival and urges the industry to present a clearer, unified message. Ripple Chief Legal Officer Stuart Alderoty is looking to federal regulators to carry crypto market rules over the finish line, arguing that Elizabeth Warren's expected rise to lead the Senate Banking Committee won't put her in charge of the industry's future. "I don’t think Elizabeth Warren is going to set crypto policy in this country," Alderoty said at The Hill and The Block’s Capitol Crypto Forum on Thursday. "She'll probably focus on oversight and hearings, which I think will be a short-term distraction." Alderoty, who also serves as president of the National Cryptocurrency Association, said he expects other lawmakers to take the wheel on crypto policy over Warren, who he described as "overtly anti-crypto." Despite this, he does not expect a version of the Clarity Act to be reintroduced in the coming Congress, pointing to a packed legislative calendar and the 2028 presidential election as priorities. Pieces of the proposal could be folded into tax legislation or other bills, he said, but a broader bill would likely struggle to garner the committee support needed to reach the floor. "I think the emphasis and the focus is going to move to the SEC and the CFTC," Alderoty said, also mentioning collaborations with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. Asked whether action from those agencies would be enough for the industry over the next two years without market structure legislation, Alderoty said: "I think it's enough, and I think it's really important." He argues that rules created through public comment and data analysis would be difficult for a future administration to reverse because they would need to carry out their own policymaking and justify disrupting the market's reliance on the existing rules, he said. Alderoty contrasted that with the approach taken by former SEC Chair Gary Gensler , arguing that reliance on enforcement left little to no durable policy when he left. "The Gensler SEC did not do the hard work of rulemaking," he said. "What they decided to do was fall back to regulation by enforcement." "This administration is doing the hard work of rulemaking, and that is durable," he added. Alderoty also pushed crypto companies to improve how they present their priorities to Congress. He cited a handful of possible reasons for the breakdown in the Clarity Act's passage, including the Senate's decision not to advance the House-passed bill, the schism between stablecoin and market structure legislation and disputes over rewards. Ethics concerns surrounding the Trump family’s crypto ties ultimately "overwhelmed the conversation," he said. The industry's competing messages also made things murky, he added, with different groups and companies all going after lawmakers with "esoteric issues" on DeFi, stablecoin rewards, and token classifications. When you consider that lawmakers' understanding of crypto can vary widely, it makes the industry's more technical pitches hard to follow. Alderoty likened the situation to a policymaker telling him about fishermen coming in to discuss fishing laws, tackle and tides that the lawmaker didn't understand. items.content:
오픈AI가 AI 모델로 AMD 주력 GPU의 회로 설계를 최적화해 전력·성능·면적(PPA) 지표에서 최대 14%의 개선을 확인했다고 밝혔다. AMD 엔지니어들이 이미 최적화한 설계에서 5개월도 안 되는 기간에 약 1년 치 추가 진전을 이뤘다는 설명이다.

오픈AI는 18일(현지시간) 공식 블로그를 통해 AMD와의 협력 성과와 자체 추론 칩 ‘할라페뇨(Jalapeño)’ 개발에 AI를 활용한 결과를 공개했다.

AMD와의 협력에서는 GPU 회로의 동작을 기술한 시스템베릴로그(SystemVerilog) 기반 RTL 코드를 AI가 다시 작성하도록 했다. 시놉시스의 반도체 설계 자동화(EDA) 도구로 변경된 회로가 기존 기능을 유지하는지 검증하고, 전력과 성능·면적 사이의 절충 관계를 평가했다.

작업 대상은 AMD 엔지니어들이 수년간 최적화한 설계였다. 오픈AI는 AI가 여기서 추가 개선점을 찾아낸 성과를 “5개월도 안 되는 기간에 약 1년 치 진전을 이룬 것”이라고 평가했다. 이는 설계 개선의 규모에 대한 회사의 평가로, GPU 전체 개발 기간을 1년에서 5개월로 단축했다는 의미는 아니다.

최대 14%라는 수치도 GPU 전체 처리 성능의 향상률이 아닌 설계 블록의 PPA 개선 결과다. AMD는 일부 변경 사항을 최근 제조용으로 제출한 설계에 반영했으며, 나머지도 향후 제품에 활용할 수 있도록 설계 파일에 추가했다고 오픈AI는 설명했다. 차세대 주력 CPU의 주요 블록에서도 한 자릿수 비율의 PPA 개선을 검증했다고 덧붙였다.

Working with @AMD , our models identified up to 14% PPA improvement on flagship GPU IP in less than five months—building on designs AMD’s engineers had already spent years optimizing.

The same approach helped improve Jalapeño, our first custom inference chip, with gains verified… pic.twitter.com/nKsnM3bTXx

자체 칩 할라페뇨에서는 AI가 제안한 변경으로 벡터 연산 장치와 행렬 연산 장치의 표준 셀 면적을 각각 약 13%, 10% 줄였다고 추산했다. 해당 최적화는 실제 칩의 초기 구동 과정에서도 검증됐다는 설명이다.

오픈AI는 AMD 설계 최적화에 사용한 모델명은 공개하지 않았다. 별도로 오픈소스 RISC-V 프로세서 코어를 활용해 모델 세대별 설계 역량을 평가했으며, 기존 회로 최적화 과제에서는 ‘GPT-6.2 아스트라’가 두 코어 모두에서 가장 높은 평균 점수를 기록했다고 밝혔다. 시놉시스와 협력해 EDA 도구를 활용하는 전용 모델 ‘GPT-시놉시스’도 개발하고 있다.

이번 발표는 최근 AI를 실제 하드웨어 설계에 활용한 사례가 잇달아 공개되는 가운데 나왔다. 오픈AI는 지난 3일 아스트라를 활용한 기기 설계 실험에서 직원 2명이 일주일 안에 외장과 회로기판, 소프트웨어를 설계하고 외부 제조업체가 시제품을 제작했다고 밝혔다. 제조에 앞서 여러 차례 검토와 수정은 필요했다.

앤트로픽도 9일 '클로드 페이블 5.2'로 전자기기 3종을 설계한 결과를 공개했다. 클로드가 부품 선정과 회로기판 배치, 외장 설계, 펌웨어 작성을 수행했으며, 협력사 다이오드 컴퓨터스가 제작한 기기들은 회로 수정 없이 작동했다고 설명했다.

이들 사례는 AI의 활용 범위가 디지털 작업을 넘어 실제 기기의 설계와 제작, 성능 개선으로 넓어지고 있음을 보여준다.

items.title: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam upgrade could slip to May 2027 over compatibility concerns
items.summary: Ethereum developers are weighing changes to gas pricing proposals that could disrupt existing smart contracts, after contacting at least 50 affected companies.
items.content:
Ethereum developers are weighing changes to gas pricing proposals that could disrupt existing smart contracts, after contacting at least 50 affected companies.

Ethereum’s Glamsterdam upgrade could be pushed back as far as May 2027 if developers decide to modify its specifications to address smart contract compatibility issues, according to discussions at Thursday’s All Core Developers meeting.

Glamsterdam is a planned Ethereum hard fork aimed at increasing the network’s capacity and efficiency. However, blockchain security firm ChainSecurity warned in October that proposed changes to Ethereum’s gas pricing could disrupt existing smart contracts and potentially expose them to exploitation, prompting developers to postpone the Hoodi testnet fork, originally scheduled for Oct. 26.

The concerns center on gas repricing proposals EIP-8037 and EIP-8038 . Researchers identified 13 real-world examples of potentially affected contracts in October, while a November investigation examined eight smart contract invariants that could be disrupted by the upgrade.

During Thursday’s meeting, developers said the Ethereum Foundation, ChainSecurity and security firm Dedaub had collectively contacted at least 50 affected companies. Three projects were classified as high impact, with fixes completed or expected by mid-December, while medium-impact projects reported timelines extending to Jan. 10.

Developers debated whether to retain Glamsterdam’s existing specifications or modify them to reduce compatibility risks , as changes intended to protect some contracts could disrupt others.

“Every spec change could, again, break new invariants that we are not aware of breaking yet,” one developer warned during the meeting.

Under the current specifications, mainnet activation could come as early as mid-January 2027. However, waiting until January to decide could push activation to late February or early March, or April or May if modifications are adopted, and no decision has been reached yet.

Related: Vitalik ‘pivots’ ETH to store of value, crypto suffers after US midterms: Hodler’s Digest

Separately, Ethereum’s next planned hard fork, Hegotá, could see its scope reduced as the network seeks to accelerate its transition to post-quantum cryptography.

During the meeting, developers considered postponing some Ethereum Improvement Proposals to prioritize post-quantum features, although several argued that reducing the upgrade’s scope would offer little benefit unless it also shortened the rollout timeline.

Developers also raised compatibility concerns over EIP-8151 , a proposal designed to protect accounts migrating to post-quantum security. A preliminary review identified a potentially large number of existing smart contracts that could be affected by the changes, complicating the proposal’s inclusion in Hegotá.

No decision was reached on Hegotá’s scope, with client teams expected to submit their positions ahead of further discussions in two weeks.

items.content:
Transport for London breach exposes 265,000 Oyster card users' data

Transport for London (TfL) has announced that around 265,000 Oyster photocard customers may have had their account details exposed in a data breach.

TfL is London's public transport authority, operating the Underground, Overground, buses, trams, and the Elizabeth line. It recorded 3.53 billion passenger journeys in 2025/26, including 1.78 billion bus journeys and 1.20 billion Tube journeys.

Oyster photocards are travel smartcards with the holder's photo that give eligible passengers free or discounted travel.

The organization discovered the security incident on November 16, 2026, after receiving customer reports about emails requesting them to create an account, which came directly from TfL's mail systems as a result of a compromise.

The Oyster photocard website has now been taken offline and the organization is sending impacted individuals data breach notifications.

Oyster photocards remain valid for travel, and customers who need to renew their cards or check their journey history can still do so by contacting TfL's Customer Services.

These notifications, with one shared on Reddit , state that the following customer data may have been exposed:

TfL's current assessment is that passwords, bank and payment card details, journey information, and the names and dates of birth of children with Zip Oyster cards were not compromised.

The transportation organization also said it has found no evidence so far that the affected data has been misused.

TfL estimates that around 265,000 photocard customers may have been impacted, up from an estimated 250k previously, but the investigation is not yet complete and the figure may increase further.

TfL says it has now contained the incident and contacted affected customers. It has also notified the UK's Information Commissioner's Office (ICO).

Those who received the previous email urging them to create an account on the platform should ignore it.

The leak of security questions and answers is particularly concerning, as those may be used in account access restoration, so customers should remain vigilant for suspicious activity and report it to the organization as soon as possible.

Once the Oyster photocard portal is restored, all photocard customers will be prompted to change their password, security question, and answer.

However, if those same security questions are used at other sites, they should be rotated to new questions and answers.

It is also recommended to change passwords on other services where the same information was used.

In 2024, Scattered Spider members breached TfL's network and stole customer data and disrupted online services , including Oyster refunds.

The attack cost the agency £29 million in losses and recovery costs, while two of the hackers pleaded guilty in June 2026 and were sentenced to five years and six months in prison.

items.title: Trump's Democratic SEC pick suggests tokenization policy deserves full rule process
items.content:
Consensus Hong Kong Prices Increase Friday

Consensus Hong Kong Prices Increase Friday

Kristin Johnson, who is expected to join the Securities and Exchange Commission soon as its lone Democrat, argued for revisiting the agency's tokenization "innovation exemption" as a full-fledged rule rather than exemption, she said in a Thursday Senate hearing to evaluate President Donald Trump's nominees for the commission .

When asked about dozens of companies objecting to having their stock offered through the SEC's new approach to tokenization, which was granted as an exemption to standing securities regulations, she said she'd "welcome the opportunity" to get the topic into a formal rulemaking that carries a public comment period, "especially when the stakeholders we see raising concerns are in fact market participants, registrants themselves."

"I feel strongly that regulation is made better through the notice-and-comment period, and in fact, it is a requirement by this body that that is how independent federal market regulators approach their responsibility to develop regulation," said Johnson, who had previously served on the Commodity Futures Trading Commission until last year and was — with Republican pick Steven Levine — nominated to join the SEC last week.

On the same topic, which was one of the SEC's most consequential policy decisions so far for the crypto industry, Levine said that the exemption was time-limited and narrow and that "many innovations, such as the exchange traded fund, began as a series of exemptive orders that ultimately resulted in agency rulemaking."

That's what SEC Chairman Paul Atkins said the agency has in mind, doing a formal rule after testing the waters with the exemption.

At the confirmation hearing for Johnson and Levine before the U.S. Senate Banking Committee, the two were among five nominees, including for roles at the Treasury Department and Department of Transportation. The SEC is meant to be a five-member commission, and the two nominees would double its current number to four — three Republicans and one Democrat.

"Artificial intelligence, tokenization, stablecoins, and decentralized platforms promise lower costs

and wider access, and they also raise real questions about conflicts of interest, data governance, and accountability," said Johnson, who has been a professor at George Washington University Law School after leaving the CFTC last year, in her prepared remarks . "In digital asset markets, I have focused on strong governance, conflicts of interest rules, and segregation of customer assets."

She and Levine also fielded questions about prediction markets firms, which Senator Catherine Cortez Masto, a Nevada Democrat, accused of illegally trading " security-based swaps as equity-based perpetuals" in relation to the CFTC's recent allowance for single-stock perpetual futures. Levine didn't commit to a position, and Johnson said there are "very critical and important questions here regarding the jurisdiction and authority of the commission."

The banking panel was instrumental in this year's failed negotiations over the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act — a process Democratic Senator Mark Warner called "a year in crypto hell" — but it's unlikely that the incoming Democrat majority will be as immediately keen on picking up the industry's top priority. Senator Elizabeth Warren, the committee's ranking Democrat who is expected to take over the chairmanship once her party takes the majority in January, has been among the Senate's loudest crypto skeptics.

Warren greeted Levine with skepticism in her opening remarks, asking, "How can we possibly believe that if you are confirmed as an SEC commissioner, that you won't be just another pawn who will put Wall Street profits over protecting American investors?"

A treasury company can have years of dividends covered and still struggle to sell new shares on terms that make another Bitcoin purchase worthwhile.

Rising US interest rates could slow buying by Bitcoin treasury companies long before they have trouble paying their bills.

Strategy raised $244.7 million by selling common stock in the week ended Nov. 15. It spent $206.3 million of the proceeds buying back preferred shares and $33.4 million on 485 BTC.

At the time, its US dollar assets covered more than three years of preferred dividends and debt interest at current payouts. When Treasury bills pay more, investors can demand a higher yield to buy newly issued preferred shares.

For common stock, StoneX analyst Mark Palmer watches how much investors will pay above the value of the Bitcoin each share represents. At a premium, a company can issue stock and buy enough Bitcoin ( BTC ) to leave shareholders with more BTC per share. However, as that premium narrows, so does the gain.

items.title: Google gives Gemini the ability to use your Mac for you
items.summary: Google's latest update to Gemini brings an AI agent to the Mac that can organize files, fill out forms, and tackle multistep workflows.
items.content:
Google on Thursday announced that it is bringing computer use to its Gemini desktop application on macOS, allowing its AI to complete tasks on users’ behalf, navigating native Mac apps, and browsing websites in the background.

The tech giant is a little late to the game with this launch, as other leading AI model makers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta have already been offering agentic features in their desktop applications for some time. Meanwhile, Google only this week announced the broader rollout of Gemini’s “Tasks,” the in-app feature that allows the AI to work more as an agent, helping users sign into websites, make online purchases, or book appointments.

Google also only recently began admitting early testers to try its revamped “CC” AI agent, announced in September , which is designed to help families stay organized across email, calendars, chats, and tasks.

Computer use is another type of agentic offering that allows an AI agent to take actions directly on the user’s computer — in Gemini’s case, a Mac. This allows the AI to complete multistep tasks that involve getting things done across local files, apps, and the web. After the user instructs the AI what they want to do, they’ll see the agent working in a live preview in their chat, while still keeping their screen and cursor free to continue working on other things.

As with other AI agents offering computer use, users can pause, stop, and approve Gemini’s actions before they happen.

Google suggests the feature could be useful for tedious tasks and other workflows, like filling out forms, repeating the same task over and over across a batch of files, organizing files into folders based on specific criteria, creating slideshows from files or information in online dashboards, and more.

The feature is initially available in English in the U.S. and requires the Gemini app for Mac and a Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscription. The company didn’t say when it would expand to other markets or platforms.

items.title: DOJ, DHS partner on new unit tackling scams and cybercrime
items.summary: The departments are partnering on the Threat Disruption Center to better triage victim complaints, map cybercriminal networks and provide a direct channel to private sector organizations that work with victims.
items.content:
Image: Dynamic Wang via Unsplash/DOJ/DHS DOJ, DHS partner on new unit tackling scams and cybercrime

The Department of Justice and Department of Homeland Security announced Thursday the creation of a new task force aimed at disrupting the flow of victim funds to foreign criminal networks powering scams, cybercrime and sextortion schemes that target Americans.

The departments are partnering on the Threat Disruption Center to better triage victim complaints, map cybercriminal networks and provide a direct channel to private sector organizations that work with victims.

Senior FBI official Heith Janke said Threat Disruption Center members have already worked together on efforts to warn thousands of victims before they lose money to scammers, and the center will allow them to better coordinate their efforts.

“The Threat Disruption Center builds on those efforts by providing advanced tools and operational capabilities that enable faster action at greater scale, strengthening the work of every agency on the task force,” Janke said.

TRM Labs, which is providing technology support for the effort, said that the center has already moved to take down more than 1,600 scam websites, added more than 6,600 scam-linked cryptocurrency wallet addresses to a screening network and identified 101 new fraud networks for investigation.

The center is part of the federal government’s efforts to implement an executive order issued in March centered around stopping cyber scams, which continue to siphon billions of dollars each year from unwitting Americans.

Cyber scam losses reported to the FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) grew to $20.9 billion in 2025 — a number that does not account for the thousands of people who never file victim reports.

The staggering losses have prompted multiple concurrent efforts by the federal government and Congress to disrupt the scams and provide better avenues for victims to report crimes .

Much of the center's work will focus on collaborating with tech companies that get a firsthand view on criminal network activity because of how many gangs use social media platforms, web hosting, domain infrastructure, cryptocurrency services and banking systems.

“The Center establishes a standing mechanism for law enforcement and participating companies to appropriately share intelligence in near real-time, and convert that intelligence into action, for example, by pausing victim payments; taking down malicious web domains; or banning social media accounts used by scammers,” federal officials said in a statement.

“Participating private-sector companies can take these actions independently under their terms of service, while law enforcement agencies proceed with investigations, prosecutions, and court-authorized seizures.”

The center is being housed within the Homeland Security Task Force — a permanent interagency law enforcement network of more than 30 federal agencies and over 440 state and local partners that focus on transnational criminal organizations, cartels and foreign terrorist organizations.

The initiative is just one part of a multi-prong effort the U.S. is undertaking to address cyber scams. On Thursday, for example, the Treasury Department issued more sanctions on scam operators in Myanmar and affiliates of the Prince Group, a Cambodian company accused of managing an empire of scam centers across Southeast Asia.

The sanctions include Zhao Hui, a Cambodian national who leased a scam center from Prince Group and paid the company fees to run the compound. U.S. officials accused Zhao of being directly involved in the scam center’s operations — which targeted Americans and Europeans with cryptocurrency investment scams.

Two of Hui’s companies, Bei Fang Bo Lin Construction Decoration and ZHZ Investment, are included in the sanctions.

items.title: CISA nominee LoSapio vows to bolster cyber defenses while denying Jan. 6 Capitol attack
items.summary: President Donald Trump’s pick to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency pledged to lawmakers to uncover any “gaps” within the organization while also denying the Capitol came under attack on January 6, 2021.
items.content:
Image: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency nominee Michael LoSapio speaks during a confirmation hearing on November 19, 2026. CISA nominee LoSapio vows to bolster cyber defenses while denying Jan. 6 Capitol attack

President Donald Trump’s pick to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency on Thursday vowed to uncover any “gaps” within the organization that have been created by massive personnel and funding cuts.

“I'm going to get involved and understand where the gaps are and I will come back to this committee with the gap analysis,” Mike LoSapio, Palantir’s chief information security officer, told the Senate Homeland Security Committee.

LoSapio was nominated earlier this month to helm the nation’s cyber defense agency, which has been without a Senate-confirmed chief for almost two years. A previous nominee, Sean Plankey, withdrew from consideration earlier this year after spending months in limbo on Capitol Hill. Nick Andersen has led CISA in an acting capacity since February.

The agency has been a target of Trump’s ire over the role it played in debunking the conspiracy theories he spread that the 2020 presidential election was rigged. Since he returned to the Oval Office, CISA has lost one-third of its staff and had its budget slashed by millions.

In a brief nomination hearing, LoSapio described CISA as “effectively the cybersecurity version of the 911 system. You pick up the phone, you say you have an emergency, you need help.”

“If confirmed, I intend to bring together the community and the national labs to help collaborate and coordinate and to give defenders the tools they need to defend their networks,” including AI tools, he told the panel.

In his written statement to the committee , LoSapio also pledged to “recruit and keep talented people, give them clear priorities, and make sure every dollar Congress provides is spent with discipline and tied to measurable results.”

However, he demurred when asked to weigh in on the recent technical outages that have upended key sectors of the U.S. as he’s “not inside” the agency today. And he stopped short of saying CISA’s budget needed to be increased to meet digital threats.

“I don't necessarily believe more money means more security. I believe spending money on the right solutions in the right ways actually decreases risk,” LoSapio told Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.).

He later testified that if analysis showed the need for more funding he would “come back to this committee and request for more resources.”

When asked by Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) who won the 2020 presidential election, LoSapio repeatedly declined to directly answer.

“I'm not going to answer the question about an election six years ago,” he said. “My only involvement in the 2020 election was voting for the president of the United States.”

LoSapio also disagreed with Blumenthal when the policymaker asked if the Capitol was attacked on January 6, 2021.

“No, I don't believe there was an attack. No,” he said under persistent questioning.

In response, Blumenthal told LoSapio he was “disqualified from the position that you've been nominated to fill.”

The committee likely won’t vote on LoSapio’s nomination until after next week’s Thanksgiving recess. If advanced, he could face a full floor vote during the final weeks of the lame-duck session of Congress.

is the senior cybersecurity reporter for The Record. Prior to joining Recorded Future News in 2021, he spent more than five years at Politico, where he covered digital and national security developments across Capitol Hill, the Pentagon and the U.S. intelligence community. He previously was a reporter at The Hill, National Journal Group and Inside Washington Publishers.

items.title: phpAfterShell Explained: How Hackers Could Turn a PHP Session Flaw Into Code Execution
items.summary: PHP's default file-based session storage can be made to return objects an attacker chose, by cutting off a session write at the right moment. When combined with a second weakness, such as a suitable gadget chain in the app, those objects can allow the attacker to run code on the
items.content:
PHP's default file-based session storage can be made to return objects an attacker chose, by cutting off a session write at the right moment. When combined with a second weakness, such as a suitable gadget chain in the app, those objects can allow the attacker to run code on the server.

Today's PHP releases fix the flaw, called phpAfterShell .

The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-126714 and rated 9.2 out of 10 on the CVSS 4.0 scale by PHP's maintainers. Depthfirst, a security company, says it found the flaw and reported it to the maintainers.

The October 21 PHP releases, which fixed two critical flaws known as PHP2Shell , do not contain this fix. Servers updated then remain affected until they install today's releases. Neither the maintainers nor the company reports any attacks using phpAfterShell.

These releases are affected, according to the maintainers' security advisory :

PHP 8.6.0, also released today, includes the fix.

The flaw is in the files session handler, which PHP uses by default. Sessions kept in Redis, a database, or another store are outside this defect, though each store's handling of a cut-off update needs its own check.

Whether an attacker needs to log in depends on how the app exposes its session handling.

On the path the company tested, the attacker uses upload progress, a PHP feature that records the progress of a file upload in the user's session. Where the feature is on, a multipart form upload that carries its field makes PHP write to the session before the app's own code runs. The app does not need an upload page, only any page that opens the session later.

PHP 8.1 and older are end-of-life. The official end-of-life mitigation branches for 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1 are not affected, but older unpatched builds of those versions are, according to the company.

The company's remediation guidance sets out these steps:

If you cannot update yet and your app does not use upload progress, set session.upload_progress.enabled = 0 in php.ini or the server's PHP settings, then restart the PHP workers. Also limit the untrusted data your app stores in sessions.

Switching the feature off is not a full fix. It closes the upload path, but apps that put attacker-controlled data into sessions in other ways remain affected, the maintainers say.

The maintainers listed the same setting on October 21 as a temporary measure for one of the PHP2Shell flaws. Servers that have kept it off since then still need the update.

Moving sessions to a store that replaces records in one step also avoids this defect. The update is still the recommended fix for sites that keep the files handler.

Linux distribution packages may include the fix without changing the PHP version number, according to the company, so the version number alone may not indicate whether a server is fixed.

Once installed, the fixed releases empty the session file before each write and stop the write if that step fails. A cut-off write can still lose session data, but it can no longer leave old data behind for an attacker to use.

The updates also switch upload progress off by default. The Hacker News compared PHP's source code for the October 21 releases and today's. The built-in setting is on in 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12, and off in 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13 and 8.6.0.

The release notes do not mention or explain the change. The sample php.ini files still show the old setting in a commented-out line. A php.ini file, distribution package, or hosting panel that switches the setting on will keep it on.

Where nothing else sets it, apps that rely on upload progress will need it switched back on after the update.

The same releases also fix other PHP security flaws .

The attack starts with the session write that upload progress makes before the app's code runs, Depthfirst's researchers say in their technical analysis .

배재대학교에서 외부 해킹 공격으로 학습관리시스템(LMS)과 연계 학사시스템에 저장된 학생·교직원 개인정보가 유출되는 사고가 발생했다. 유출 정보에는 학번과 사번, 성명, 이메일 등 기본 개인정보뿐 아니라 사용자 계정과 비밀번호 관련 정보까지 포함돼 추가적인 계정 탈취 위험에 대한 조사가 필요한 상황이다.

배재대학교는 11월 18일 오후 2시 45분 공식 홈페이지에 '개인정보 유출 사실 안내 및 사과문'을 게시했다. 해당 공지는 대학 시설안전처 정보관리팀 명의로 등록됐다.

이번 사고는 11월 16일 오전 9시부터 오후 11시 12분 사이 발생한 외부 해킹 공격과 관련된 것으로 파악됐다. 침해 대상은 학생들의 온라인 강의와 학습 활동을 지원하는 LMS와 이에 연계된 학사시스템이다.

현재까지 공개된 사고 내용에 따르면 LMS에서는 학번·사번, 성명, 이메일, 소속, 최종 접속일 등의 개인정보가 유출된 것으로 파악됐다.

연계 학사시스템에서는 사용자 ID, 암호화된 비밀번호, 해킹 ID, 영문 비밀번호, 로그인 ID, 생년월일 등의 정보가 유출 항목으로 알려졌다.

특히 비밀번호 관련 정보가 유출 항목에 포함됐다는 점은 주목할 부분이다. 암호화된 비밀번호와 별도로 기재된 '영문 비밀번호'가 실제 평문 비밀번호를 의미하는지, 과거 시스템에서 사용하던 별도 인증정보인지에 따라 피해 위험이 달라질 수 있다.

다만 현재 확보한 자료만으로 비밀번호가 복호화 가능한 형태로 유출됐거나 공격자가 실제 계정에 로그인했다고 단정할 수는 없다. 정확한 비밀번호 저장 방식과 유출된 인증정보의 성격은 추가 확인이 필요하다.

대학 측은 주민등록번호, 여권번호, 운전면허번호, 외국인등록번호 등 고유식별정보는 유출되지 않았다는 입장을 밝힌 것으로 알려졌다. 현재까지 정확한 피해 인원과 유출 건수는 확인되지 않았다.

배재대는 침해사고에 대응하기 위해 피해 시스템 2대를 외부망에서 격리하고 포털 시스템 로그인 시 2차 인증을 의무화하는 등 보안 강화 조치에 나선 것으로 파악됐다.

계정정보 유출에 따른 추가 피해를 막기 위해 일부 사용자를 제외한 계정의 비밀번호를 일괄 초기화하고, 개인정보보호위원회와 한국인터넷진흥원(KISA)에 사고를 신고한 것으로 알려졌다.

피해 대상자에게는 개별 통지를 진행하고 본인의 개인정보 유출 항목을 확인할 수 있는 조회 기능도 제공하는 것으로 파악됐다.

다만 대학이 공격을 최초 인지한 정확한 시각과 공격자의 침입 경로, 실제 개인정보 반출 방식은 확인되지 않았다. 공격자가 LMS와 학사시스템 가운데 어느 시스템에 먼저 접근했는지, 두 시스템 사이의 연계 기능이 공격에 이용됐는지도 추가 조사가 필요한 부분이다.

이번 사고는 최근 국내 대학에서 개인정보 유출과 연구행정시스템 침해사고가 잇따르는 가운데 발생했다는 점에서도 주목된다.

대학의 학습관리시스템은 학생과 교수자의 강의 활동을 지원하지만, 학사시스템과 연계되는 과정에서 학번, 소속, 이메일, 계정정보 등 다양한 개인정보를 처리한다. 이러한 연계 구조에서는 하나의 시스템에 대한 침해가 다른 시스템의 개인정보 노출로 확대될 가능성이 있다.

특히 이번 사고에서는 학습 활동에 필요한 기본정보 외에 로그인 ID와 비밀번호 관련 정보가 유출 항목에 포함된 것으로 알려져 계정 보안에 대한 면밀한 점검이 요구된다.

공격자가 확보한 인증정보를 이용해 다른 학내 서비스에 접근할 수 있었는지, 동일한 비밀번호를 사용하는 외부 서비스로 피해가 확산될 가능성이 있는지도 확인해야 한다.

최근 발생한 대학 산학협력단 연구비관리시스템 해킹 사건과의 연관성도 조사 대상이 될 수 있다. 그러나 현재까지 배재대 사고가 동일한 공격자나 취약점에 의해 발생했다는 사실은 확인되지 않았다.

이번 사고는 대학의 온라인 교육과 학사행정 시스템이 단순한 학습 지원 도구를 넘어 학생과 교직원의 개인정보를 집중적으로 처리하는 주요 정보자산이라는 점을 보여준다. 정확한 피해 규모와 최초 침투 경로를 규명하는 한편, LMS와 학사시스템 사이의 접근권한 관리 및 인증정보 보호체계를 점검할 필요가 있다.

items.content:
PHP security updates fix 18 flaws, including critical RCE bugs

The PHP dev team released security updates for 18 vulnerabilities, including critical flaws that could allow unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute code on vulnerable servers.

The updates were released Thursday, November 19, for all supported PHP branches, with PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, and 8.2.36 now available.

Security firm Aikido reports that the updates address 18 CVEs affecting PHP's core engine, session handling, PHP-FPM, CGI, and other components.

One of the most serious flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-129289, is a critical PHP-FPM request smuggling vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.2.

According to Aikido, the flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to execute PHP code remotely on vulnerable servers that reuse connections to PHP-FPM under certain conditions.

The vulnerability affects certain nginx, Apache, HAProxy, and LSAPI configurations that reuse backend connections to PHP-FPM.

Standard nginx and Apache configurations that do not reuse backend connections are not affected by the attack.

Other important vulnerabilities fixed in the updates include:

CVE-2026-129474: A use-after-free vulnerability involving magic method backtraces that could lead to remote code execution.

CVE-2026-129496: A timezone cache use-after-free vulnerability that could lead to remote code execution.

CVE-2026-126714: A vulnerability involving partially overwritten session files that could lead to remote code execution.

CVE-2026-115560: A session serializer mismatch vulnerability that could lead to remote code execution.

CVE-2026-129291: A PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free vulnerability that could lead to local privilege escalation.

CVE-2026-128090: A PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass vulnerability involving an algorithm downgrade.

Additional fixes address memory corruption, information disclosure, cross-site scripting, denial-of-service issues, and potentially unsafe handling of HTTPS and FTPS URLs.

The releases follow a warning issued Wednesday by the PHP security team that the upcoming updates would address vulnerabilities affecting all supported PHP versions, with the highest severity rated critical.

"The issues rated CRITICAL require either non-default configuration or uncommon setups," the PHP security team warned .

One of the vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-115560, was already disclosed in an October 23 informational advisory and relates to how PHP handles session data under certain configurations, potentially leading to remote code execution.

As a temporary mitigation, PHP recommended disabling session upload progress by setting session.upload_progress.enabled=0 and restarting PHP workers. This setting was also recommended to mitigate the recent PHP2Shell flaws .

For CVE-2026-129289, administrators who cannot immediately install the security updates can mitigate the vulnerability by disabling persistent backend connections between their web servers and PHP-FPM, ensuring connections are closed after each request.

Aikido warns that these mitigations do not address all vulnerabilities fixed in the November updates and recommends ensuring PHP-FPM and LSAPI listeners are not directly exposed to untrusted networks.

Although the official security updates are limited to supported PHP branches, third-party maintainer Ondrej Surý has also released patched packages for unsupported PHP versions dating back to PHP 5.6.

Aikido has similarly released hardened PHP container images containing backported security fixes for unsupported versions, including PHP 5.6, 7.0, 7.1, 7.2, 7.4, and 8.1.

PHP administrators are urged to upgrade to PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, or 8.2.36, depending on their supported branch, to address the newly disclosed vulnerabilities.

items.title: UK court confirms British government served Apple with secret encryption notice
items.summary: The British government served Apple with a secret legal notice targeting the company’s cryptographic protections for iCloud accounts, a tribunal has confirmed, ending almost two years of official refusal to acknowledge what had been widely reported.
items.content:
Image: Gian Paul Guinto / Unsplash UK court confirms British government served Apple with secret encryption notice

The British government served Apple with a secret legal notice targeting the company’s cryptographic protections for iCloud accounts, a tribunal has confirmed, ending almost two years of official refusal to acknowledge what had been widely reported.

In a judgment handed down Thursday, the Investigatory Powers Tribunal — the only court in the country that can hear certain national security cases — rejected the government’s “neither confirm nor deny” policy based on the argument that even confirming the existence of the notice would damage national security.

The court’s three judges stated explicitly that the government “has given Apple a technical capability notice,” referencing the legal power which the government used to demand that Apple retain the ability to access the content of iCloud accounts.

At the core of the dispute is Apple’s Advanced Data Protection (ADP) feature which generates and stores encryption keys on users’ own devices instead of Apple’s servers. Because Apple never holds the keys, it is technically unable to access the content of iCloud accounts even when served with a lawful request.

Last February, Apple withdrew ADP for British users entirely after receiving the technical capability notice, as was first reported by The Washington Post. Although the details of the notice are not public, it appears that Apple effectively complied by withdrawing ADP for British users.

Since the initial report about the notice, Westminster officials have continued to repeatedly state they do “not comment on operational matters, including for example confirming or denying the existence of any such notices.”

Addressing Parliament earlier this year, Security Minister Dan Jarvis again declined to respond after the issue was raised by a lawmaker, and said that not doing so was “a long-standing position held by successive Governments for obvious reasons of national security.”

Those “obvious reasons” were challenged by the tribunal, as well as in comments from both within the U.K. intelligence community and from academic experts.

In a preliminary judgment last April, the tribunal cited numerous public comments by senior U.S. politicians, including President Donald Trump, that appeared to confirm the existence of the notice, with Trump comparing the British government’s move to “something that you hear about with China.”

The then-U.S. Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard ordered a legal review of the secret directive in February 2025, and said she had a “grave concern” about its implications. In its judgment, the tribunal also referenced numerous British media reports about the notice, citing government officials as sources, as additional justification for finding against the “neither confirm nor deny” policy.

Experts, including from Britain’s own intelligence community, have argued the government’s attempts to access encrypted messaging platforms should be more transparent. Academics described the Home Office's ongoing refusal to either confirm or deny the legal demand as unsustainable and unjustifiable.

Tim Stevens, the head of the King's Cyber Security Research Group at King's College London, previously told Recorded Future News that a default of no comment left the government unable to control the story when details came out.

Sir Jeremy Fleming, the former director of GCHQ, told the Munich Cyber Security Conference in 2025 that greater transparency was needed to protect the agencies’ “license to operate.”

In 2018, GCHQ technical officials argued in an essay for Lawfare that the details of any exceptional access scheme would probably become public anyway, and that criminals would not simply switch services once it was known to exist. The tribunal found that confirmation of a notice’s existence would not tell adversaries anything that they could not already find elsewhere.

중소기업중앙회가 운영하는 소기업·소상공인 공제제도 '노란우산'에서 고객 개인정보와 계약정보 총 36만여 건이 외부 비인가자에게 조회돼 유출된 사실이 공식 확인됐다. 유출 정보에는 고객의 이름과 연락처뿐 아니라 사업장 정보, 공제 납부 내역, 개인 이체은행과 계좌번호까지 포함돼 있어 2차 금융사기 피해에 대한 우려가 커지고 있다.

중소기업중앙회는 11월 18일 '노란우산 개인정보 유출 및 침해사고 공지'를 추가 게시하고 외부 전문기관의 정밀검사 결과를 공개했다. 앞서 14일에는 노란우산 홈페이지에서 고객 개인정보가 제3자에게 조회됐을 가능성이 있다고 안내했으나, 이번 조사에서 실제 개인정보 유출 사실이 확인된 것이다.

중소기업중앙회에 따르면 사고는 지난 11월 10일 발생했다. 외부 비인가자가 노란우산 홈페이지에 비정상적으로 접근했으며, 정밀검사 결과 고객 개인정보와 계약정보 총 36만여 건을 무단 조회한 것으로 확인됐다.

이번에 유출된 정보는 고객명, 주민등록번호 앞 6자리, 휴대전화번호, 자택 주소와 전화번호, 이메일 등 기본 개인정보다. 고객번호와 계약번호, 청약번호, 문자메시지(SMS) 및 이메일 수신 동의 여부도 포함됐다.

특히 사업장명, 사업자번호, 개업일자, 사업장 주소, 사업장 전화번호와 팩스번호 등 사업 운영과 관련된 정보도 유출됐다.

금융 관련 정보도 상당 부분 포함됐다. 월부금액, 부금 납부일, 부금 납부 월수, 납부 총금액 등 공제 납부 내역과 개인 이체은행 및 계좌번호가 유출 대상에 포함된 것으로 확인됐다.

다만 중소기업중앙회는 주민등록번호 뒷자리는 암호화 처리돼 유출되지 않았다고 설명했다. 공지에 나열된 정보가 모든 피해자에게 동일하게 유출된 것은 아니며, 개인별 유출 항목에는 차이가 있다.

중소기업중앙회는 유출 대상 고객에게 개별 문자메시지를 발송했으며, 노란우산 홈페이지 공지 화면에서 본인의 개인정보 유출 항목을 직접 확인할 수 있도록 했다.

이번 사고에서 주목할 부분은 일반적인 고객 연락처를 넘어 공제 계약정보와 납부 내역, 금융계좌 정보까지 함께 노출됐다는 점이다.

공격자가 확보한 정보가 실제 금융사기에 악용될 경우 고객의 이름과 사업장 정보, 공제 가입 내역 등을 활용해 중소기업중앙회나 노란우산 관계자를 사칭하는 정교한 공격이 가능하다.

예를 들어 공제 납부금액이나 계약번호 등 실제 고객정보를 언급하며 납부 계좌 변경, 환급금 지급, 공제대출 신청 등을 유도할 경우 피해자가 정상적인 안내로 오인할 위험이 있다.

특히 노란우산은 소기업·소상공인의 생활 안정과 사업 재기를 지원하는 공제제도라는 점에서 유출된 사업장 정보와 금융정보가 결합될 경우 피해자의 경제활동과 직접 관련된 2차 피해로 확대될 가능성을 배제할 수 없다.

중소기업중앙회는 이번 사고와 관련해 전화나 문자메시지로 금전이나 대출을 요구하거나 납부 계좌 변경, 계좌 비밀번호 입력을 요구하지 않는다고 강조했다. 노란우산 홈페이지는 계좌 비밀번호를 수집하지 않으며, 고객에게 홈페이지 아이디나 비밀번호를 요구하는 일도 없다고 밝혔다.

고객들에게는 출처가 불분명한 문자메시지와 이메일의 링크를 클릭하거나 개인정보 및 금융정보를 입력하지 말 것을 당부했다.

중소기업중앙회는 사고 확인 이후 공격에 사용된 IP 주소를 차단하고 공격 기록을 분석해 보안 정책을 강화했다고 밝혔다. 개인정보가 조회된 화면에 대한 접근통제도 강화했다.

개인정보보호위원회와 한국인터넷진흥원(KISA)에 관련 법률에 따른 신고를 완료했으며, 관계기관 조사에도 협조하고 있다고 설명했다.

피해 고객은 노란우산 고객센터(1666-9988)나 전용 이메일(privacy_check@kbiz.or.kr)을 통해 사고 관련 문의와 피해 신고를 할 수 있다. 개인정보 유출로 피해가 발생한 경우 개인정보 분쟁조정위원회에 분쟁조정을 신청하거나 관련 법률에 따른 손해배상을 청구할 수 있다.

중소기업중앙회는 "이번 사안을 매우 엄중하게 받아들이고 있으며, 재발 방지를 위해 필요한 조치를 다하겠다"고 밝혔다.

items.content:
케이사인(대표이사 구자동·최현철)이 11월 19일 오크우드 프리미엄 인천 프리미어룸에서 열린 ‘2026 가천대학교 기반구축사업단 & 스마트홈케어 산업 글로벌 협력 네트워크 컨퍼런스’에서 가천대학교 총장상을 받았다.

이번 행사는 가천대학교 지능형홈케어 통합지원 기반구축사업단이 그간의 성과를 나누고 스마트홈 헬스케어 산업의 방향과 글로벌 협력을 논의하기 위해 마련됐다. 행사에는 국내외 연구기관과 기업, 관련 기관 전문가들이 모여 인공지능(AI)과 스마트홈 기반 헬스케어 기술의 산업화 가능성과 협력 방안을 살폈다.

케이사인은 가천대학교 기반구축사업단이 추진하는 취약계층 친화적 홈케어 서비스 개발 및 실용화 기반구축사업에 협력 파트너로 참여했다. 사업단이 만든 AI 시스템의 프라이빗 클라우드 환경에서 암호화와 보안 시스템 전반을 컨설팅하고 구축한 공로를 인정받아 총장상 수상자로 선정됐다.

스마트홈 헬스케어 분야는 기기와 서비스 전반에서 건강과 생활 정보 같은 민감한 데이터를 모으고 활용한다. 이 때문에 AI 시스템과 클라우드 인프라에서 데이터를 안전하게 지키는 일이 중요하다. 케이사인은 초기 단계부터 보안 요구사항을 따져 프라이빗 클라우드 환경에 맞는 암호화·보안 체계를 설계하고 구축해 AI 시스템 운영의 토대를 다졌으며, 민감 데이터를 다루는 연구·서비스 환경의 신뢰도를 높였다.

케이사인은 이번 수상을 계기로 스마트홈 헬스케어를 비롯한 AI 산업 전반에서 데이터 보호를 지원하는 보안 파트너 역할을 이어갈 방침이다.

구자동 케이사인 대표이사는 “스마트홈 헬스케어처럼 민감한 데이터를 다루는 AI 산업에서는 보안이 곧 신뢰의 출발점이라고 생각한다”며 “가천대학교 기반구축사업단과 함께한 프로젝트를 높이 평가해 주셔서 감사드린다. 앞으로도 AI 시대에 안전한 데이터 활용 환경을 만드는 데 필요한 기술과 경험을 나누겠다”고 말했다.

items.title: PHP Patches Seven Critical RCE Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Successful exploitation could allow attackers to crash the worker process and execute code with the PHP worker’s privileges. The post PHP Patches Seven Critical RCE Vulnerabilities appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.content:
PHP on Thursday rolled out a fresh set of security patches as part of its four-week update schedule, including fixes for seven critical-severity remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities.

First in line is CVE-2026-115560 , which was publicly disclosed last month, two days after PHP2Shell patches landed. Residing in the session upload progress feature, it could be triggered to write attacker data using one session serialization format and then read it using another.

“A mismatched decoder can interpret part of a session key as serialized object data. An application with a suitable object gadget chain can then execute code with the privileges of the PHP worker,” PHP’s advisory reads.

Next in line is CVE-2026-129481 , described as a use-after-free that occurs after a session shutdown has been interrupted, and which PHP describes as an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-109619, one of the two PHP2Shell flaws fixed in October and now widely exploited.

“An attacker who can cause an application’s session cleanup to fail in this way may corrupt memory or crash a reused PHP worker. The use-after-free could potentially lead to remote code execution, but code execution through this specific field has not been demonstrated,” PHP notes, adding that PHP 8.2 is not affected.

Another use-after-free, CVE-2026-129182 , covers additional exploitation scenarios for CVE-2026-109619, an RCE via stale global state. According to PHP, however, RCE via these scenarios has not been demonstrated. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

Impacting PHP 8.5 and later, CVE-2026-129474 is a use-after-free weakness that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to cause a fatal error and achieve RCE. “Exploitation depends on the application and requires control over enough request data to influence memory allocation, a reachable magic method call, and a fatal error at the relevant point,” PHP says.

Attackers able to influence session contents and interrupt the write of serialized data to a session file may trigger the deserialization of attacker-controlled content when the session is next opened. Tracked as CVE-2026-126714 , the flaw could lead to RCE via a suitable object gadget chain in the application.

PHP also patched CVE-2026-129289 , a PHP-FPM request smuggling issue caused by PHP reading a request-body stream lazily, treating a request body as handled during request shutdown and skipping the normal cleanup that discards unread input.

“PHP can fail to discard unread bytes from an HTTP request body before reusing a persistent PHP-FPM or LSAPI connection. In PHP-FPM, an unauthenticated attacker can make those bytes form a separate FastCGI request, bypass front-end routing and execute attacker-controlled PHP code with the privileges of the worker,” PHP explains.

The seventh critical-severity vulnerability patched today, CVE-2026-129496 , resides in the timezone cache. PHP can retain a reference to it when writing a diagnostic to a PHP error log file during process startup, and a later diagnostic can access the freed cache before it is reset.

“On affected configurations, a remote attacker can trigger memory corruption, cause a worker to crash, and potentially execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the PHP worker,” PHP explains.

PHP 8.6.0 and PHP 8.5.13 were rolled out with fixes for all critical bugs and for 10 high and medium-severity flaws. Patches for most issues were also included in PHP 8.4.28, PHP 8.3.37, and PHP 8.2.36. More information is available on PHP’s news archive page.

발표를 맡은 더존비즈온 AX지원본부 이성재 수석컨설턴트는 AI 도입의 핵심 요소로 기술 자체보다 업무 설계를 꼽았다. 기업 AI 에이전트 사업의 88%가 실제 운영에 이르지 못한다는 해외 분석(Digital Applied)을 들며, 모델 성능보다 업무 규칙이 AI가 이해할 수 있는 형태로 정리되지 않은 점이 걸림돌로 작용한다고 짚었다.

행정 현장의 적용 방향도 구체화됐다. 미국 스탠퍼드대학 연구에서 노동자들이 세무·법무 보조처럼 반복 업무를 AI에 맡기려는 의향을 보인 점을 언급하며, 공문서 배부와 계약 관리, 일상감사, 예산 집행, 업무추진비 관리 등 다섯 가지 행정업무를 AI 에이전트가 맡는 구상을 설명했다. 접수 문서를 분류해 배부하고, 계약법에 맞는 계약 방식과 서류를 만들며, 집행률이 낮은 예산을 찾아 집행 방안을 제안하는 방식이다.

공공기관 망분리 환경에 맞춘 Private AI 구조도 소개됐다. ONE AI PE는 외부 인터넷과 끊긴 폐쇄망 안에 거대언어모델(LLM)을 구축해 기관 데이터를 외부로 내보내지 않고 처리하는 솔루션이다. 하드웨어와 소프트웨어, 언어모델, 검색증강생성(RAG)을 기관 내부에 두고, 더존 언어모델과 업무시스템 데이터를 잇는 API 브릿지와 다중 에이전트 협업 오케스트레이션 구조를 갖췄다.

현장 부스에는 중앙부처와 지방자치단체, 공공기관 정보화 담당자들이 찾아 구매·계약 업무를 수행하는 AI 에이전트 시연을 지켜봤다.

ONE AI PE는 서울시 공공 AI 사업에 2년 연속 참여하며 현장 적용 사례를 늘리고 있다. 지난해 서울시 생성형 AI 행정 플랫폼 챗봇 2.0 구축 사업에 쓰였고, 올해는 행정지원 AI 에이전트 구축 사업에 공급돼 문서 요약과 회의실 예약, 제안서평가위원 선정 등을 돕는 AI 에이전트 공통 기반 역할을 맡았다.

더존비즈온 관계자는 "현장에서 만난 공공기관 담당자들이 AI의 실제 행정업무 처리 방식에 높은 관심을 보였다"며 "기관별 업무 절차와 기준에 맞춘 AI 에이전트로 공공기관의 AI 전환(AX)을 돕겠다"고 밝혔다.

items.content:
엔피코어(대표 한승철)가 ‘2026년 중소기업 R&D 우수성과 50선’ 공공혁신 우수성과 부문에 이름을 올렸다. 엔피코어는 11월 18일 청주 오스코(OSCO)에서 열린 ‘2026년 중소기업 R&D 우수성과 공유회 및 포상식’에 참여해 연구개발 기술과 사업화 성과를 알렸다.

행사에서 방효섭 연구기획실장은 분야별 대표기업 발표자로 나서 인공지능(AI) 기반 통합 APT 보안 기술을 설명했다. 이 기술은 네트워크, 이메일, 망연계에서 위협을 걸러내고 PC와 서버 같은 엔드포인트 보안 대응까지 하나로 잇는 구조다.

구체적인 탐지 흐름을 보면 네트워크 구간에서는 악성 URL과 명령제어(C&C) 통신을 잡아낸다. 이메일 구간은 피싱 메일과 첨부파일을 살피고, 망연계 환경은 반입·반출 파일의 안전 여부를 점검한다. 엔드포인트 구간에서는 자사 제품 ZombieZERO EDR과 맞물려 PC와 서버에서 발생하는 위협을 탐지한다.

공격 경로가 제각각인 지능형지속위협(APT)에 대응하려면 구간별 보안이 따로 놀지 않고 이어져야 한다. 엔피코어는 Inspector N·E·F와 엔드포인트 보안을 연결해 기관과 기업의 업무환경에 맞춰 적용할 수 있는 체계를 제시했다.

사업화 실적도 함께 공유됐다. 행사 기업정보 제출 자료 기준으로 엔피코어의 2021년부터 2025년까지 누적 공공매출은 52억6천만원이다. 연구개발 결과물을 실제 공공 보안 현장에 적용해 매출로 연결한 사례를 짚은 것이다.

한승철 엔피코어 대표는 “이번 선정은 연구개발을 통해 축적한 보안 기술을 실제 현장에서 활용할 수 있는 제품과 서비스로 연결해 온 노력의 성과”라며 “앞으로도 고객의 운영환경과 보안 요구에 맞는 기술 개발을 이어가겠다”고 말했다.

items.content:
The PHP Foundation has released security updates to address multiple critical security flaws that could be exploited to achieve remote code execution on affected deployments, including CVE-2026-115560.

The release of the patch follows an advance notice in which the project maintainers alerted users to multiple critical vulnerabilities affecting all supported PHP versions under specific conditions, including non-default configuration or uncommon setups.

At a high level, successful exploitation of the defects could pave the way for remote code execution, session corruption, denial-of-service, memory corruption, or local privilege escalation.

The list of vulnerabilities is as follows -

Depthfirst, which has codenamed CVE-2026-126714 " phpAfterShell ," has described it as a critical flaw that can enable a remote attacker to run arbitrary code on affected servers.

"If a pwrite()/ftruncate() update is interrupted, PHP may leave behind a malformed session file that is later loaded by session_start(), yielding an arbitrary deserialization primitive," Depthfirst said. "Chained with another of our PHP-native deserialization-to-RCE findings, this leads directly to remote code execution."

Put differently, the vulnerability turns an interrupted file write into a potential remote code execution primitive by manipulating how PHP writes session data to disk, causing it to interpret previously harmless data as executable object data.

It then exploits the unexpected session state where the PHP worker either dies while the write process is underway, leaving a partially updated file, or dies after the write is complete, but before content from the previous session is removed. Both scenarios lead to a mixture of two different session states.

"Depending on where the interruption happens, part of the new Session may already have been written while bytes from the previous Session remain on disk," security researcher Yuhang Wu said. "The result can be a Session file containing the prefix of the new serialized data and the tail of the old one."

"By carefully choosing the length fields in the new prefix, an attacker can make PHP's Session decoder interpret leftover bytes that were previously just part of an ordinary string as separate Session entries and serialized objects. Nothing needs to be deserialized during the upload-progress callback itself. The attacker only needs to leave the right bytes on disk and wait for the application to call session_start(), at which point PHP reads the modified Session and deserializes those objects."

Once the prefix of one valid session is spliced with the tail of a replacement session, a subsequent session treats the corrupted data as a legitimate server-side state. This, in turn, causes PHP to interpret it as a "different, valid Session" and ultimately enable remote code execution by chaining it with a memory-corruption in a PHP-native class.

It affects any application that runs an affected PHP version with file-based sessions. If immediate patching is not possible, it's advised to turn off session upload progress.

Patches for the flaws are available in the following versions -

Users who are using existing 8.2.x, 8.3.x, 8.4.x, and 8.5.x versions of PHP are advised to update to the latest version for optimal protection.

items.title: European Commission confirms cyberattack, says hackers used AI tool
items.summary: POLITICO had reported CERT-EU had identified the attackers’ use of ARTEX, an open-source AI hacking platform that the FBI last week warned was being used both by criminals and state-sponsored groups.
items.content:
European Commission headquarters in Brussels. Image: LIBER Europe / Flickr / CC BY 2.0 European Commission confirms cyberattack, says hackers used AI tool

The European Commission confirmed Thursday that it had been hit by a cyberattack last month involving a publicly available artificial intelligence tool, following media reports of the incident.

Speaking to journalists, Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier said the first signs of the attack were detected October 22. He described the incident as an “AI-generated cyber campaign” but did not identify the tool used or the attackers’ apparent motivation.

POLITICO first  reported that the Commission had been impacted by the cyberattack. It said CERT-EU had identified the attackers’ use of ARTEX, an open-source AI hacking platform that the FBI last week  warned was being used both by criminals and state-sponsored groups.

The attack reportedly disrupted the European Commission’s personnel systems for more than 10 days, including payroll, leave requests, medical reimbursements and translation services.

A commission spokesperson confirmed to Recorded Future News they had “taken the necessary steps in response to a detected cyber campaign,” including taking several services offline as “a protective measure.”

They said they had notified affected individuals and were “preventively checking other systems” while keeping in touch with CERT-EU and the European Data Protection Supervisor.

Regnier said investigators had found no evidence of a data breach affecting Commission staff broadly and were unaware of any ransom demand. He said the investigation remains open.

Asked why the incident was not disclosed earlier, Regnier said publicizing defensive measures could undermine their effectiveness. “There was no hiding whatsoever,” he told journalists.

The incident follows an alert issued in June by the Five Eyes intelligence alliance, which said AI would fundamentally transform both offensive and defensive cyber capabilities. “The timeline is not years, it is months,” it said at the time.

The FBI warned last week that ARTEX was being used prolifically by cybercriminals and nation-states to breach government agencies and dozens of critical sectors worldwide, “with some intrusions progressing from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours.”

The open-source framework, which was released in July, uses commercial AI models to automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation.

“The key takeaway here is not that threat actors are using Artex,” said Shaun Williams, a senior director at SentinelOne, “but that the widespread availability of AI-powered tools like Artex have allowed threat actors to find and exploit vulnerabilities in internet facing devices faster, more effectively, cheaper, and with less skill than ever before.”

The attack is the Commission's third disclosed cyber incident this year, following breaches involving  Ivanti software in January and its  cloud infrastructure in March. Officials have not linked the incidents.
